SHA updated 2026-05-29 in PR #345 (reciprocal Q-3 / Q-4 / Q-5 / C8 Category (a) edits), then re-updated post-merge 2026-05-29 to scrub the residual C8 Category (b) row referencing the closed #341 Confidential K8s wrapper. Second reviewer round 2026-05-29 in PR #345: corrected three C8 Category (a) ADR paths from the speculative working titles used at C8 authoring time to the actual committed #337 ADR filenames (FR-001 → llm-model-router-policy.md, FR-002 → persona-skill-contract.md, FR-004 → sovereignty-zdr-posture.md) so the consumer inheritance surface points at files that exist on disk (codex P2 #2). Third reviewer round 2026-05-29 in PR #345: refined the C7 Q-5 RabbitMQ queue-type pick from `quorum` to `stream` (`x-queue-type: stream`) — log-structured offset-addressable storage that natively satisfies C7 Replayability for new-subscriber catch-up without amending the sealed C7 contract (codex P2 #5). Fifth reviewer round 2026-05-29 in PR #345: reconciled C8 Category (a) inheritance honesty (codex P2 round-5 #2) — added an inheritance-mechanism preamble note explaining that `internal`-tier rows are blueprint-source-only normative references (the *rules* are inherited via the C7/C8 contract surface; the *files* are pruned at consumer init per `source_artifact_prune_globs_on_init` and absent from `template_sync_allowlist`); reclassified all 12 ADR rows (one #339 + the meta-ADR + ten #337 content ADRs) from `stable`/`sealed` to `internal`/`n/a (normative reference)` to honestly reflect that consumer repos do not receive these files; FR-004 (item 4) and FR-006 (item 5) annotations preserved with corrected wording explaining that the rule content (not the file extensibility) is sealed under FR-017(b). The per-instance parameterization callouts that previously sat on FR-003/FR-007/FR-009/FR-010 rows are now described in the preamble as inherited via the consumer-overlay surface rather than via the ADR file. Eleventh reviewer round 2026-05-30: re-enumerated C8 Category (b) `infra/modules/*` runtime wrappers to add six #334 wrappers — ske-foundation-cluster-wrapper, stackit-secrets-manager-wrapper, eso-cluster-secret-store-wrapper, logme-worm-retention-wrapper, factory-egress-networkpolicy-wrapper, factory-bot-identity-wrapper — covering the SKE foundation cluster + Secrets Manager + ESO + WORM-retention LogMe + egress NetworkPolicy + bot identity provisioning surface required by FR-019's two-emitter rule (the orchestrator and webhook handler need the SKE cluster, secrets, and egress posture before they can run). Extended the existing #335 eso-factory-binding-wrapper row description to clarify that the binding consumes the #334 ClusterSecretStore (codex P2 round-11 — #334 runtime wrapper re-enumeration in C8 Cat (b)). Twelfth reviewer round 2026-05-30: C7 schema amendment — extended the `phase` enum with `agent-pr-review` (eighth value) so the FR-008 step05 / step08 audit-pairing invariant is schema-validatable end-to-end; added an explanatory paragraph documenting the enum-naming convention (strip `step0N-` from each `blueprint-sdd-step0N-<name>` skill basename) and pinning that additions to the enum are out of scope for consumer overlays and require a #339 sign-off cycle (codex P2 round-12 — phase-enum gap). Adding an enum value extends the sealed nine-field schema in the direction permitted by C7's 'addition of further fields is permitted' clause without breaking any existing producer or subscriber. Thirteenth reviewer round 2026-05-30: two source-side C7 corrections. (a) **Trigger-acceptance handoff removed from the webhook handler's C7 events list (L307)** and reframed as a separate side-channel RabbitMQ work-queue message — design-contracts.md previously listed the `factory-trigger-accepted` label handoff among the webhook handler's C7 emissions, but `ADR-issue-337-c7-emission-mechanism.md` §:51 already described the same handoff as a RabbitMQ work-queue message that is NOT a C7 event. The two documents now match: trigger acceptance has no entry in the `phase` enum, and the first C7 event for an accepted trigger is the orchestrator's `phase: intake` event (codex P2 round-13 #1 — trigger-accepted alignment). (b) **Idempotency-identifier alignment with the sealed schema (codex P2 round-13 #2)**. The idempotency rule reads `event_id = sha256(ticket_id|phase|rerun_round|emitter)` but `event_id`, `emitter`, and `work_item_id` were not declared as required schema fields (the schema declared `ticket_id`, not `work_item_id`), leaving #333 / #336 implementers reliant on unvalidated extension fields for dedupe and FR-008 audit pairing. Fix: (i) promoted `event_id` and `emitter` to required schema fields (the schema preamble now lists eleven required fields; `emitter` is an enum (`orchestrator` | `webhook-handler`) matching the two-emitter rule from FR-019); (ii) rewrote the idempotency formula to use the schema-declared `ticket_id` instead of `work_item_id` and added a paragraph anchoring all four derivation inputs to declared schema fields; (iii) unified terminology on `ticket_id` throughout — the round-12 `agent-pr-review` enum-naming paragraph that previously referenced `work_item_id` for the FR-008 pairing description now references `ticket_id` to match the schema field name. The nine→eleven cascade was applied to: the schema `required` array, the schema preamble sentence ('nine minimum fields' → 'eleven minimum fields'), the Cross-link-to-downstream-observers paragraph at L302 ('nine-field' → 'eleven-field'), and FR-017(b) item 6 (the sealed list explicitly enumerates all eleven fields, with a parenthetical noting that `event_id` + `emitter` were added in round-13 to make the idempotency formula derivable from declared fields alone — additions are permitted by the same 'Addition is permitted' clause the item itself carries, so no contract widening is involved).
